question: Are the HronTurek FSI3/CFD3/ALE/replay results on xenosim exposed to the two defects fixed by solids4foam PR #546 (28751407c): (1) GCC -O3 tmp aliasing in nf() & (-devReff().boundaryField()) in the fluid patchViscousForce; (2) scale-dependent barycentric weights (triangle::pointToBarycentric) in the AMI point transfer? Also the further aliasing sites of the audit commit c8efdd390 (newMovingWallVelocity::snGrad, fvcGradf, mechanicalEnergies, ...).
verdict: Not exposed. The aliasing miscompilation manifests with the study toolchain (GCC 11.4 -O3) in standalone tests, but in the FSI3/CFD3/replay runs it changes nothing: A/B restarts with the fixed tree (27c9bfdf7 + 28751407c + c8efdd390) are identical to all written digits (coupled FSI3 2x 600 steps incl. the FSI residual file; replay 2x 600 steps, which uses newMovingWallVelocity; CFD3 2x 500 steps with 28751407c). The barycentric defect cannot trigger (smallest interface fan triangle 1e4 above threshold).

defect1_tmp_alias.reproducer: Test-tmpDotAlias.C / buildAliasTest.sh from origin/verification/3dtube-level3, run on xenosim with the system toolchain
defect1_tmp_alias.note_2D: platform/Test-tmpDotAlias2D.C keeps the loop structure of the reproducer and sets n_z = 0, D_xz = D_yz = 0 (D_zz != 0), as on the FSI3 plate of a one-cell-thick x-y mesh; the miscompiled loop forms z last from the overwritten normal, z = (n.D)_x D_xz + (n.D)_y D_yz, which is the exact value 0 when D_xz = D_yz = 0. A restructured variant (function called with several sizes) did not miscompile at all: code generation is context dependent, hence the A/B test.
defect1_tmp_alias.where_it_acts: pimpleFluid::patchViscousForce is called only for the fluid-to-solid traction of a coupled run; fluid-only runs (CFD3, ALE, replay) report OpenFOAM forces function-object loads and do not call it.

defect2_barycentric.threshold: 4 A^2 < SMALL = 1e-15 m^4, i.e. fan-triangle area A < 1.58e-8 m^2 (face area < 6.3e-8 m^2)
defect2_barycentric.transfer: interfaceTransferMethod not set in fsiProperties: default AMI (amiInterfaceToInterfaceMapping), point weights on fan triangles (two face vertices + face centre, area = face/4 for these rectangles)
defect2_barycentric.note: The interface faces span the 15 mm mesh depth; the in-plane edge would have to fall below about 4 micrometres to trigger the degenerate branch.
